question.text: On complete combustion of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>492</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of an organic compound containing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7938</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4428</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> was produced. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math> composition of oxygen in the compound is____. (Nearest Integer)

solution.text:
Organic compound +O2⟶  CO2g     +    H2O                                                       

                                         0.7938 gram       0.4428 gram

Number of moles of CO2=Number of moles of C

=0.793844Weight of carbon=0.79384412=0.216g

Weight of hydrogen=0.4428182=0.0491g

Weight of oxygen=0.492-0.216-0.0491=0.2269g
